bib.title: Aligning AI With Shared Human Values

read.skipped: Reference list lines skimmed only; MTurk form figures (13-22) are images with no extractable text.

question: Can language models predict widespread human moral judgments across justice, deontology, virtue, utilitarianism and commonsense morality?
hypothesis: Pretrained language models fine-tuned on scenario-based ethics data can learn some of the connection between world facts and human values, though incompletely.
contributions: ETHICS dataset of over 130,000 contextualized scenarios across five ethical perspectives, with Test and adversarially filtered Hard Test sets
Baseline results for fine-tuned BERT, RoBERTa, ALBERT and few-shot GPT-3
Analysis of a learned utility function and a disagreement-detection test bed of about 1K contentious examples

method.summary: Crowdsourced (MTurk) and Reddit-derived text scenarios are cleaned by multi-annotator consensus, contrast-set construction and adversarial filtration with distilBERT/distilRoBERTa. Transformers are fine-tuned on the Dev set per task and scored on Test and Hard Test; GPT-3 is evaluated few-shot.
method.task: Binary moral-judgment classification (justice, deontology, virtue, commonsense) and pairwise utility ranking (utilitarianism)

datasets.name: ETHICS
datasets.size: over 130,000 examples; Dev/Test/Hard Test per task (Table 1)
datasets.split: Dev (fine-tune); Test; adversarially filtered Hard Test. Justice 21791/2704/2052, Virtue 28245/4975/4780, Deontology 18164/3596/3536, Utilitarianism 13738/4808/4272, Commonsense 13910/3885/3964
datasets.source: Amazon Mechanical Turk (US, Canada, Great Britain English speakers, Spring 2020) plus long Commonsense scenarios from the AITA subreddit via PRAW; no licence stated
datasets.preprocessing: Consensus relabeling (5 MTurkers, keep >=4/5 agreement for Justice, Deontology, Commonsense; 3 MTurkers unanimous for Virtue traits; 7 MTurkers majority on adjacent comparisons for Utilitarianism); Reddit posts kept with >=100 votes and >=95% agreement, balanced, politically/sexually charged and edited posts removed; adversarial filtration with 5 repeated 0.8n/0.2n splits of distilBERT+distilRoBERTa, keeping highest-loss examples

datasets.name: Contentious Commonsense Morality
datasets.source: Long Reddit scenarios with 50% +/- 10% vote agreement

models.name: Word averaging (GloVe)
models.architecture: average of 100-dim GloVe vectors plus affine map

training.objective: Binary classification cross-entropy (Justice, Deontology, Virtue, Commonsense); pairwise loss -log sigma(U(s1)-U(s2)) for Utilitarianism
training.optimizer: Transformers: not stated. Word averaging: Adam
training.lr: grid {1e-5, 3e-5} for Transformers; 1e-3 (Adam default) for word averaging
training.seq_len: 64 max tokens per input; 512 for Commonsense Morality
training.seeds: best result across all runs reported; number of seeds not stated

other.hyperparameter_selection: grid search using the normal Test set

inference.samples: GPT-3 few-shot; 32 examples for Justice, Deontology, Virtue, short Commonsense; 8 short examples for long Commonsense; utilitarianism uses 5 in-prompt rated examples
inference.prompting: Few-shot templates in Appendix B; Utilitarianism has GPT-3 rate each scenario 1-10 independently and ranks by rating

metrics.name: 0/1-loss accuracy
metrics.definition: Commonsense and Utilitarianism: per-example/per-pair accuracy. Justice, Deontology, Virtue: a model is correct only if it classifies all related examples in the group correctly

metrics.name: AUROC (disagreement detection)
metrics.definition: Predictive uncertainty used to separate contentious from clear-cut Commonsense scenarios; 50% is chance

eval.protocol: Best exact-match percentage across all runs on Test and Hard Test; no significance test stated

prompts.text: Rate how pleasant each of the following activities is on a scale from 1 (very unpleasant) to 10 (very pleasant). Followed by five rated Activity examples (ratings 7, 5, 3, 8, 2).

Few-shot GPT-3 averages 39.3 on Test and 32.3 on Hard Test, worse than fine-tuned Transformers on Test but competitive on Hard Test Utilitarianism and Commonsense.
Word-averaging baseline is the worst model, barely above random on the Test average.

results.quote: BERT-large had an AUROC of 58%, RoBERTa-large had an AUROC of 69%, and ALBERT-xxlarge had an AUROC of 56%.

limits: Data comes from English speakers in the US, Canada and Great Britain, so it reflects Western moral views; Indian annotator agreement is 93.9% on Commonsense.
Dataset covers clear-cut scenarios only, not moral dilemmas or contentious topics.
Hyperparameters were chosen by grid search on the normal Test set and the best run is reported, so Test numbers are optimistically selected; number of seeds not stated.
Dev set is not large enough to load ethical knowledge into a model; the dataset measures but does not teach ethics.
Authors state the work is only a first step; models tested are pre-2021 (BERT-family, GPT-3), so numbers have dated for current LLMs.
Dataset datasheet says it is not intended for ambiguous dilemmas and may identify Reddit posters; no plans to update.
